steps.message:
# Task

Submission TO-2026-0447 goes to the bindery on Friday and the thesis office needs a full
pre-binding pass over it first. Everything is in `input/`: the section log exported from the
typesetting system, the part plan naming the template each part is set in, the template
profiles, our DFS-12 standard, its amendments, and the office's record of this submission.

Apply the standard as written. Several limits are per-template, so a section is only in
breach against the template its own part is set in, and the parts carry a rule of their own.

## Deliverable 1 — `formatting_audit.csv`

One row per audited section, with these columns in this order:

    section_id,part_id,template_id,finding

`finding` carries the code for every rule that section breaches, joined with `|` and no
spaces, in the order the standard sets them out:

    MARGIN_NONCOMPLIANT | TYPE_AREA_INVALID | LEADING_NONCOMPLIANT | FONT_NONCOMPLIANT
    | HEADING_STYLE_INVALID | CAPTION_MISSING | NUMBERING_INVALID

Use `none` for a section that breaches nothing. Rows may be in any order.

## Deliverable 2 — `part_summary.csv`

One row per part, with these columns in this order:

    part_id,template_id,section_count,flagged_sections,start_page,pagination

`section_count` and `flagged_sections` count audited sections. `start_page` is the page the
part opens on. Use the same `none` convention in `pagination` for a part that paginates
cleanly.

## Deliverable 3 — `formatting_memo.md`

A markdown memo for the thesis officer. Say which amendments you applied and which you did
not, naming each by its identifier and giving your reason in each case, and give the value of
every figure you derived from the standard and used as a threshold — the numbers, not just
the method, and both numbers where a figure differs between the two templates. Say how many
log rows you audited and how many you set aside, and on what basis. Account for every section
carrying a finding, naming it by `section_id` and giving, for each of its findings, the
measured value and the limit it missed. Where a section's numbers look like a breach and the
standard clears it anyway, say what clears it. Call out the sections whose release from the
type-area rule turns on which template their part is set in. Name the parts that cannot be
paginated as planned and the page each one currently opens on. And give the total number of
captions still to be written across the batch.

---
Save your deliverables into your current working directory using exactly these filenames:
    - `formatting_audit.csv` — Per-section formatting audit
    - `part_summary.csv` — Per-part rollup
    - `formatting_memo.md` — Markdown memo
    - `results.json` — a JSON object whose values are all integers, with the keys
      `section_count`, `part_count`, `clean_section_count`, `flagged_section_count`,
      `finding_total` (every finding raised across the batch, not the number of sections
      carrying one), `margin_count`, `type_area_count`, `leading_count`, `font_count`,
      `heading_count`, `caption_missing_count`, `numbering_count` (each of these seven
      counting the audited sections carrying that finding), `caption_shortfall_total` (how
      many captions the batch is missing in total, across the sections carrying
      `CAPTION_MISSING`), `pagination_invalid_parts` (how many parts cannot be paginated as
      planned), `sections_in_invalid_parts` (how many audited sections sit in those parts),
      `flagged_archive_sections` and `flagged_reading_sections` (flagged sections split by
      the template their part is set in)
- Writing those files is the required deliverable and must be your final action; confirm each one exists before you answer.

---

## Working environment

- Your current working directory is `/app`, and it is writable.
- The read-only attachments referred to as `input/` are at `/app/input`.
- Write every deliverable into `/app`, at the exact filenames listed above.

<content>
1: # DFS-12 — dissertation formatting standard
2: 
3: Graduate Thesis Office, revision 12. Supersedes DFS-11. This is the standard the
4: thesis office's pre-binding audit is run against.
5: 
6: DFS-12 is amended from time to time. The amendments are published separately in
7: `dfs12_amendments.md`, each carrying its own effective date. **An amendment governs
8: over this base text from its effective date onward.** An amendment whose effective
9: date falls after the dissertation's date of submission is not yet in force and has
10: no bearing on the audit, however recently it was published.
11: 
12: ## §1 Scope and how findings are reported
13: 
14: Every section of the dissertation is checked against §2 to §8. Every part is checked
15: against §9.
16: 
17: A section carries one finding code for each rule it breaches. A section may breach
18: several rules at once and every breach is reported; a section that breaches none is
19: reported as clean.
20: 
21: Two of the limits below are **per template** rather than a single office-wide number.
22: A section takes its template through its part: `part_plan.csv` names the template for
23: each part, and `template_profiles.csv` holds that template's limits. A section must
24: be judged against the template its own part is set in.
25: 
26: **Revisions.** The section log is an export from the typesetting system and carries
27: every revision of a section that was re-typeset during correction. Only the
28: **highest-numbered revision** of each `section_id` is audited; lower-numbered
29: revisions are superseded and are retained for history only. A superseded revision
30: contributes nothing to the audit — not a finding, not a page, not a count. The
31: export is not sorted and row position carries no meaning.
32: 
33: ## §2 Margins — `MARGIN_NONCOMPLIANT`
34: 
35: Margins are recorded per side. **Inner** is the binding edge.
36: 
37: - `margin_top_cm` and `margin_bottom_cm` must each be **not less than the template's
38:   `min_top_bottom_cm`**.
39: - `margin_inner_cm` must be not less than the binding-edge minimum. The base text sets
40:   that minimum at 2.5 cm; see the amendments.
41: 
42: A section short on any of those three is `MARGIN_NONCOMPLIANT`. A section exactly at a
43: minimum is compliant.
44: 
45: ## §3 Type area — `TYPE_AREA_INVALID`
46: 
47: The outer margin is not recorded directly. It is what is left of the page once the
48: binding edge and the text block are taken off, and it is the figure that decides
49: whether the outer edge is wide enough:
50: 
51:     implied outer margin = page width − margin_inner_cm − text_block_width_cm
52: 
53: The dissertation is printed on A4. A portrait page is **21.0 cm** wide and a landscape
54: page is **29.7 cm** wide; take the width from the section's own `orientation`.
55: 
56: A section whose implied outer margin is **less than the template's `min_outer_cm`** is
57: `TYPE_AREA_INVALID`. Exactly at the minimum is compliant. Work to two decimal places.
58: 
59: **Exception — landscape data annexes.** A section is released from §3, and from §3
60: only, where **all three** hold:
61: 
62: 1. its `section_type` is `annex`;
63: 2. its `orientation` is `landscape`; and
64: 3. it carries an **oversized table** — its `widest_table_cm` is greater than the type
65:    area a landscape page would otherwise allow under this standard, that being the
66:    landscape page width less the binding-edge minimum and less the template's
67:    `min_outer_cm`.
68: 
69: That allowance is not the same number for both templates. The exception releases the
70: section from §3 and from nothing else; in particular the binding-edge minimum in §2 is
71: not subject to this or any other exception.
72: 
73: ## §4 Leading — `LEADING_NONCOMPLIANT`
74: 
75: Line spacing is recorded as a leading, in `leading_unit` (`pt` or `mm`) and
76: `leading_value`. **For the purposes of this standard 1 pt is 0.35 mm**, so a leading
77: recorded in millimetres is converted to points by dividing by 0.35.
78: 
79: The required leading is **1.5 times the body size this standard requires**, which is
80: 1.5 × 12.0 pt = **18.0 pt** — irrespective of the size a section actually uses. A
81: section set at some other size does not get a proportionally smaller leading; it gets
82: a §5 finding and a §4 finding.
83: 
84: A section whose converted leading differs from the requirement by more than 0.05 pt is
85: `LEADING_NONCOMPLIANT`.
86: 
87: ## §5 Body font — `FONT_NONCOMPLIANT`
88: 
89: Every section must set its body text in Times New Roman at **12.0 pt**. Both halves
90: apply to every section, annexes included.
91: 
92: A section whose `body_font_name` is not an accepted identifier, or whose
93: `body_font_size_pt` is not 12.0, is `FONT_NONCOMPLIANT`.
94: 
95: **Appendix F — accepted font identifiers.** These, and only these, denote the Times
96: New Roman face for the purposes of DFS-12:
97: 
98: - `Times New Roman`
99: - `TimesNewRomanPSMT`
100: - `Times New Roman PS MT Std`
101: 
102: Metrically compatible substitutes are not the face itself and are not accepted.
103: `Nimbus Roman No9 L`, `Liberation Serif` and `Tinos` are substitutes.
104: 
105: ## §6 Heading style — `HEADING_STYLE_INVALID`
106: 
107: Headings must be set in the same face as body text — that is, `heading_font_name` must
108: also be one of the Appendix F identifiers — and must be large enough to read as a
109: heading.
110: 
111: A heading is large enough when `heading_font_size_pt` is at least the template's
112: `min_heading_step_pt` above **the size the section's body text actually uses**, not
113: above the size §5 requires. Exactly at that figure is compliant.
114: 
115: A section failing either half is `HEADING_STYLE_INVALID`.
116: 
117: ## §7 Captions — `CAPTION_MISSING`
118: 
119: Every float — every figure and every table — must carry a caption. `float_count` is
120: the number of floats in the section and `caption_count` the number of captions.
121: 
122: A section whose `caption_count` is less than its `float_count` is `CAPTION_MISSING`.
123: The difference is that section's **caption shortfall**: the number of captions still
124: to be written.
125: 
126: ## §8 Page numbering — `NUMBERING_INVALID`
127: 
128: Each part is numbered in one style throughout, given as `numbering` in
129: `part_plan.csv`. A section whose `page_number_style` is not the style its own part is
130: numbered in is `NUMBERING_INVALID`.
131: 
132: ## §9 Pagination — `PAGINATION_INVALID`
133: 
134: Every part must open on a **recto**, that is on an odd-numbered page.
135: 
136: Pages run continuously from page 1 through the whole dissertation in `sequence` order.
137: A part's start page is therefore one more than the total page extent of every audited
138: section that sits before it in `sequence`:
139: 
140:     start page of a part = 1 + Σ page_extent of all audited sections of lower sequence
141: 
142: Count the pages actually present in the audited batch; do not take an extent on trust
143: from a superseded revision. A part whose start page is even is `PAGINATION_INVALID`
144: and has to be repaginated before binding.
145: 
146: §9 is a property of the part, not of any one section in it. A `PAGINATION_INVALID`
147: part is not a finding against its sections.
148: 
149: ## Waivers
150: 
151: The thesis office may grant a section a standing waiver of a named rule. Waivers in
152: force for this dissertation are listed in the submission record. A waiver clears the
153: finding it names, within the scope it names, and does nothing outside that scope.
154: 
155: ## Finding codes
156: 
157: Section: `MARGIN_NONCOMPLIANT`, `TYPE_AREA_INVALID`, `LEADING_NONCOMPLIANT`,
158: `FONT_NONCOMPLIANT`, `HEADING_STYLE_INVALID`, `CAPTION_MISSING`, `NUMBERING_INVALID`.
159: Part: `PAGINATION_INVALID`. Clean: `none`.

(End of file - total 159 lines)
</content>

1: # DFS-12 amendments
2: 
3: Graduate Thesis Office. Amendments to the base standard, in order of issue.
4: 
5: Each amendment states its own **effective date**. An amendment is in force for a
6: dissertation if its effective date falls on or before that dissertation's date of
7: submission. An amendment that is not in force has no bearing on the audit, however
8: recently it was published.
9: 
10: ---
11: 
12: ## A-1 — binding-edge margin
13: 
14: **Effective 2024-06-01.**
15: 
16: §2's minimum for the **inner** (binding-edge) margin is raised from 2.5 cm to
17: **2.8 cm** for every section, so that text is not lost into the gutter when the volume
18: is bound. The minima for the top and bottom margins are unchanged and remain the
19: template's own figure.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## A-2 — binding-edge margin, revised
24: 
25: **Effective 2025-01-15.**
26: 
27: **A-1 is superseded in full and ceases to have effect on this date.** Trial binding of
28: the 2024 intake showed 2.8 cm to be insufficient for volumes over 300 pages. §2's
29: minimum for the **inner** margin is **3.0 cm** for every section.
30: 
31: This figure is also the binding-edge minimum §3 uses when working out the type area a
32: landscape page would otherwise allow.
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## A-3 — landscape data annexes, narrowed
37: 
38: **Effective 2025-09-01.**
39: 
40: §3's exception for landscape data annexes was being read too broadly. It applies only
41: where all three of the conditions listed in §3 hold, and it releases the section from
42: §3 alone. The binding-edge minimum in §2 is not subject to it.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## A-4 — leading for body sections
47: 
48: **Effective 2026-07-01.**
49: 
50: §4's required leading for sections of `section_type` `body` becomes **double**, that
51: is 2.0 × 12.0 pt = 24.0 pt. Front matter, back matter and annexes are unaffected and
52: remain at 18.0 pt.
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## A-5 — leading recorded in millimetres
57: 
58: **Effective 2025-11-01.**
59: 
60: Leading may be recorded in millimetres as well as points. The conversion for the
61: purposes of this standard is **1 pt = 0.35 mm**, and the requirement is unchanged: it
62: is 1.5 times the body size the standard requires, irrespective of the size a section
63: actually uses.

(End of file - total 63 lines)
</content>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import csv, json

INPUT = "/app/input"
OUT = "/app"
SUBMISSION_DATE = "2026-03-09"

# ---- amendments in force (effective <= submission date) ----
# A-1 effective 2024-06-01  (superseded in full by A-2 on 2025-01-15) -> not applied
# A-2 effective 2025-01-15 <= 2026-03-09 -> IN FORCE  : inner margin 3.0 cm
# A-3 effective 2025-09-01 <= 2026-03-09 -> IN FORCE  : landscape annex exception narrowed
# A-4 effective 2026-07-01 >  2026-03-09 -> NOT IN FORCE : body leading stays 18.0 pt
# A-5 effective 2025-11-01 <= 2026-03-09 -> IN FORCE  : mm leading, 1 pt = 0.35 mm
BINDING_EDGE_MIN = 3.0          # A-2
PT_PER_MM = 0.35                 # A-5 : 1 pt = 0.35 mm  -> mm/0.35 = pt
REQUIRED_LEADING_PT = 18.0       # A-4 not in force
LEADING_TOL = 0.05
REQUIRED_BODY_SIZE = 12.0
PAGE_WIDTH = {"portrait": 21.0, "landscape": 29.7}
ACCEPTED_FONTS = {"Times New Roman", "TimesNewRomanPSMT", "Times New Roman PS MT Std"}

# ---- waivers (in force iff submission date <= expiry) ----
# W-1 SEC-AN-01  §5 font-id only  expires 2026-12-31 -> in force
# W-2 SEC-AN-05  §5 font-id only  expires 2026-01-31 -> EXPIRED (2026-03-09 > 2026-01-31)
# W-3 SEC-LOF    §3 type area     expires 2026-11-30 -> in force
# W-4 SEC-CH07   §7 captions      expires 2026-06-30 -> in force
WAIVER = {
    "SEC-AN-01": "FONT",
    "SEC-LOF":   "TYPE_AREA",
    "SEC-CH07":  "CAPTION",
    # SEC-AN-05 W-2 expired -> not entered
}

FINDING_ORDER = [
    "MARGIN_NONCOMPLIANT", "TYPE_AREA_INVALID", "LEADING_NONCOMPLIANT",
    "FONT_NONCOMPLIANT", "HEADING_STYLE_INVALID", "CAPTION_MISSING",
    "NUMBERING_INVALID",
]
CODE_INDEX = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(FINDING_ORDER)}

# ---------------- read inputs ----------------
parts = {}
with open(f"{INPUT}/part_plan.csv") as f:
    for r in csv.DictReader(f):
        parts[r["part_id"]] = {"name": r["part_name"], "template_id": r["template_id"], "numbering": r["numbering"]}

templates = {}
with open(f"{INPUT}/template_profiles.csv") as f:
    for r in csv.DictReader(f):
        templates[r["template_id"]] = {
            "name": r["template_name"],
            "min_top_bottom_cm": float(r["min_top_bottom_cm"]),
            "min_outer_cm": float(r["min_outer_cm"]),
            "min_heading_step_pt": float(r["min_heading_step_pt"]),
        }

rows = []
with open(f"{INPUT}/dissertation_section_log.csv") as f:
    for r in csv.DictReader(f):
        rows.append(r)

# keep highest revision per section_id
latest = {}
for r in rows:
    sid = r["section_id"]
    if sid not in latest or int(r["revision"]) > int(latest[sid]["revision"]):
        latest[sid] = r
audited = list(latest.values())
superseded_rows = len(rows) - len(audited)

def fnum(x):
    return None if x == "" else float(x)

# ---------------- per-section audit ----------------
results = {}   # sid -> dict
for r in audited:
    sid = r["section_id"]
    pid = r["part_id"]
    tpl_id = parts[pid]["template_id"]
    tpl = templates[tpl_id]
    findings = {}  # code -> detail dict

    top = float(r["margin_top_cm"]); bottom = float(r["margin_bottom_cm"]); inner = float(r["margin_inner_cm"])
    tbw = float(r["text_block_width_cm"])
    widest = fnum(r["widest_table_cm"])
    orient = r["orientation"]
    stype = r["section_type"]
    bfont = r["body_font_name"]; bsize = float(r["body_font_size_pt"])
    hfont = r["heading_font_name"]; hsize = float(r["heading_font_size_pt"])
    lunit = r["leading_unit"]; lval = float(r["leading_value"])
    fcount = int(r["float_count"]); ccount = int(r["caption_count"])
    pstyle = r["page_number_style"]
    extent = int(r["page_extent"]); seq = int(r["sequence"])

    # ---- §2 margins ----
    fails = []
    if top < tpl["min_top_bottom_cm"] - 1e-9:
        fails.append(("top", top, tpl["min_top_bottom_cm"]))
    if bottom < tpl["min_top_bottom_cm"] - 1e-9:
        fails.append(("bottom", bottom, tpl["min_top_bottom_cm"]))
    if inner < BINDING_EDGE_MIN - 1e-9:
        fails.append(("inner", inner, BINDING_EDGE_MIN))
    if fails:
        findings["MARGIN_NONCOMPLIANT"] = {"fails": fails}

    # ---- §3 type area ----
    pw = PAGE_WIDTH[orient]
    outer = round(pw - inner - tbw, 2)
    type_breach = outer < tpl["min_outer_cm"] - 1e-9
    exception_applied = False
    if stype == "annex" and orient == "landscape" and widest is not None:
        thr = round(29.7 - BINDING_EDGE_MIN - tpl["min_outer_cm"], 2)
        if round(widest, 2) > thr + 1e-9:
            exception_applied = True
            type_breach = False
    waiver_cleared_ta = False
    if type_breach and WAIVER.get(sid) == "TYPE_AREA":
        type_breach = False
        waiver_cleared_ta = True
    if type_breach:
        findings["TYPE_AREA_INVALID"] = {"outer": outer, "min_outer": tpl["min_outer_cm"]}

    # ---- §4 leading ----
    if lunit == "mm":
        conv = round(lval / PT_PER_MM, 6)
        recorded = f"{lval} mm"
    else:
        conv = round(lval, 6)
        recorded = f"{lval} pt"
    diff = round(abs(conv - REQUIRED_LEADING_PT), 6)
    if diff > LEADING_TOL + 1e-9:
        findings["LEADING_NONCOMPLIANT"] = {"converted": conv, "recorded": recorded, "diff": diff}

    # ---- §5 font ----
    font_reasons = []
    if bfont not in ACCEPTED_FONTS:
        font_reasons.append(("name", bfont))
    if abs(bsize - REQUIRED_BODY_SIZE) > 1e-9:
        font_reasons.append(("size", bsize))
    if font_reasons and WAIVER.get(sid) == "FONT":
        font_reasons = []  # W-1/W-2 clear the font-identifier half only; size still required
        # re-check size alone (waiver clears identifier only, not size)
        if abs(bsize - REQUIRED_BODY_SIZE) > 1e-9:
            font_reasons = [("size", bsize)]
    if font_reasons:
        findings["FONT_NONCOMPLIANT"] = {"reasons": font_reasons}

    # ---- §6 heading ----
    head_reasons = []
    if hfont not in ACCEPTED_FONTS:
        head_reasons.append(("name", hfont))
    step = round(hsize - bsize, 6)
    if step < tpl["min_heading_step_pt"] - 1e-9:
        head_reasons.append(("step", hsize, bsize, step, tpl["min_heading_step_pt"]))
    if head_reasons:
        findings["HEADING_STYLE_INVALID"] = {"reasons": head_reasons}

    # ---- §7 captions ----
    if ccount < fcount:
        if WAIVER.get(sid) != "CAPTION":
            findings["CAPTION_MISSING"] = {"floats": fcount, "captions": ccount, "shortfall": fcount - ccount}

    # ---- §8 numbering ----
    if pstyle != parts[pid]["numbering"]:
        findings["NUMBERING_INVALID"] = {"page_style": pstyle, "part_style": parts[pid]["numbering"]}

    ordered = sorted(findings.keys(), key=lambda c: CODE_INDEX[c])
    results[sid] = {
        "section_id": sid, "part_id": pid, "template_id": tpl_id,
        "sequence": seq, "page_extent": extent,
        "findings": findings, "ordered": ordered,
        "type_area_exception": exception_applied,
        "type_area_waiver": waiver_cleared_ta,
        "outer": outer, "min_outer": tpl["min_outer_cm"],
    }

# ---------------- pagination (§9) ----------------
by_seq = sorted(audited, key=lambda r: int(r["sequence"]))
# part -> list of audited sections
part_secs = {pid: [] for pid in parts}
for r in by_seq:
    part_secs[r["part_id"]].append(r)

part_start = {}
for pid in parts:
    secs = sorted(part_secs[pid], key=lambda r: int(r["sequence"]))
    min_seq = int(secs[0]["sequence"])
    before = sum(int(s["page_extent"]) for s in by_seq if int(s["sequence"]) < min_seq)
    part_start[pid] = 1 + before

# ---------------- write formatting_audit.csv ----------------
with open(f"{OUT}/formatting_audit.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["section_id", "part_id", "template_id", "finding"])
    for r in sorted(results.values(), key=lambda x: x["sequence"]):
        finding = "|".join(r["ordered"]) if r["ordered"] else "none"
        w.writerow([r["section_id"], r["part_id"], r["template_id"], finding])

# ---------------- write part_summary.csv ----------------
with open(f"{OUT}/part_summary.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["part_id", "template_id", "section_count", "flagged_sections", "start_page", "pagination"])
    for pid in sorted(parts):

    f = r["findings"]["MARGIN_NONCOMPLIANT"]["fails"]

    for edge, val, lim in f:
        if edge == "inner":
            out.append(f"inner (binding-edge) margin {val:.2f} cm against the {lim:.1f} cm binding-edge minimum set by A-2")
        else:
            out.append(f"{edge} margin {val:.2f} cm against the template's min_top_bottom_cm {lim:.1f} cm")
    return "; ".join(out)

def ta_detail(r):
    f = r["findings"]["TYPE_AREA_INVALID"]
    raw = rows[r["section_id"]]
    pw = 21.0 if raw["orientation"] == "portrait" else 29.7
    inner = float(raw["margin_inner_cm"]); tbw = float(raw["text_block_width_cm"])

            f"against min_outer_cm {f['min_outer']:.2f} cm")

def lead_detail(r):

# Formatting audit memo — TO-2026-0447

**Candidate:** R. Okonkwo-Bailey. **Dissertation:** *Sediment transport under intermittent flow regimes*. **Date of submission:** 2026-03-09. **Standard:** DFS-12, as amended. **Binding:** hardbound, single volume, inner edge.

This memo records the pre-binding audit run against the standard as written. All thresholds below are the figures derived from DFS-12 and actually used as limits in this audit; where a limit differs between the two templates both numbers are given.

## Amendments applied

The dissertation was submitted 2026-03-09. An amendment is in force where its effective date falls on or before that date; one whose effective date falls after the submission date is not yet in force and is not applied.

- **A-1 — not applied.** A-1 (binding-edge margin 2.8 cm, effective 2024-06-01) is *superseded in full* by A-2 and ceases to have effect on 2025-01-15. It therefore has no independent bearing on this audit.

- **A-2 — applied.** Effective 2025-01-15, on or before the submission date. It sets the §2 inner (binding-edge) margin minimum at **3.0 cm** for every section, and supplies the 3.0 cm binding-edge minimum that §3's landscape exception works from.

- **A-3 — applied.** Effective 2025-09-01, on or before the submission date. It narrows §3's landscape-annex exception to the three conditions in §3 and confirms the exception releases a section from §3 only; the §2 binding-edge minimum is not subject to it.

- **A-4 — not applied.** Effective 2026-07-01, which is **after** the 2026-03-09 submission date, so it is not yet in force. The §4 required leading therefore stays at 1.5 × 12.0 pt = **18.0 pt** for every section, including body sections (which A-4 would have raised to 24.0 pt). This is why SEC-CH09, a body section set at 24.0 pt, is still a leading breach.

- **A-5 — applied.** Effective 2025-11-01, on or before the submission date. It allows leading to be recorded in millimetres and fixes the conversion at **1 pt = 0.35 mm** (a millimetre value is divided by 0.35 to get points); the requirement itself is unchanged at 18.0 pt.

## Thresholds used (the figures, not the method)

Per-section limits taken from the template the section's own part is set in:

| Figure | TPL-ARCHIVE | TPL-READING |
|---|---|---|
| min_top_bottom_cm (top & bottom margin, §2) | 2.5 cm | 2.0 cm |
| min_outer_cm (outer margin, §3) | 2.5 cm | 2.0 cm |
| min_heading_step_pt (heading step above the body size the section actually uses, §6) | 2.0 pt | 1.0 pt |

Office-wide figures (same for both templates):

- Binding-edge (inner) margin minimum, §2: **3.0 cm** (set by A-2; the base text's 2.5 cm no longer applies).

- Required leading, §4: **18.0 pt** (1.5 × 12.0 pt; A-4 not in force). Tolerance ±**0.05 pt**.

- mm→pt conversion, §4/A-5: divide the millimetre value by **0.35**.

- Required body font, §5: Times New Roman at **12.0 pt**. Accepted identifiers: `Times New Roman`, `TimesNewRomanPSMT`, `Times New Roman PS MT Std` (metrically compatible substitutes such as Nimbus Roman No9 L, Liberation Serif and Tinos are not the face and are not accepted).

- Pagination, §9: a part must open on a **recto** (odd page). Start page = 1 + Σ page_extent of every audited section of lower sequence; extents are taken only from the audited (highest) revision.
